title: M0: Spike: the drum rack preset (.adg) anatomy, from files saved by the DAW
description:
## Purpose

Answer, with real files saved by the DAW, exactly what a drum rack preset (`.adg`) must contain for a kit to load with the right pads, pitches, levels and warping, before any spec or product code is written. The `.alc` clip format is owned by the sidecar initiative (apricitus-d7746d); this spike only confirms the parts the clip folder relies on (clip name, info text, region, file reference) and reuses that initiative's findings (its spike is apricitus-9fb5fe; the set export's is apricitus-f838a3) if they have already run.

## Questions the spike answers

1. Minimal preset: the root element's version attributes, the drum group device, one branch per pad, and which elements the DAW refuses to load without.
2. Pad notes: how a branch's receiving note is stored (plain MIDI note or an inverted value), and the default note for pad 1 (expected C1 = 36).
3. Sampler per pad: root key, transpose, detune (cents), volume (linear or dB), sample start/end (frames), playback mode (classic with note-off vs one-shot), release, loop off.
4. Warping inside the sampler: are warp markers written the same way as in a clip (seconds to beats), and which warp modes exist there.
5. File references: absolute path, relative path, or both; does the DAW relink by relative path when the preset sits in a user library folder; are size/CRC fields required.
6. Velocity: the sampler's velocity-to-volume setting that comes closest to Apricity's velocity curve (`velocity_db`, 100 = matched level, 127 about +4 dB, 40 about -16 dB).
7. Clip file (confirm only): clip name, info text, start/end/loop region, warp on/off for an unwarped sample.

## Artifact it leaves (no product code)

- `design/daw-presets.md`: an annotated minimal XML skeleton for the preset, the field-by-field mapping table (kit -> rack), the answers above, and a Mermaid diagram of the document tree.
- Reference files saved by the DAW under `crates/apricity-daw/tests/fixtures/reference/` (gzipped XML only, pointing at audio paths; no audio in git).

## Definition of Done

- Every question above has an answer backed by a reference file.
- The owner has decided the open questions recorded on the initiative (pad note layout, MIDI file vs MIDI clip, reference vs copy audio).
- Applies: design note (6), fixtures (5), running log (10). Specs, code, schema, CLI, docs, web: not applicable (spike).

## Dependencies

- Shares findings with the sidecar spike (apricitus-d7746d) and the set export (apricitus-6edba8); whichever runs first writes the shared file-reference and warp-marker sections.

comments.text:
## Where reference files come from (decided 2026-09-26)

Checked: the DAW is not installed on the owner's Mac, and neither the persistent library (~5,500 files) nor the production bucket holds any `.als`, `.alc`, `.adg` or `.asd`. So this spike must NOT depend on the owner saving files. Instead:

1. **Public reference files.** Gather sets, clips, presets and sidecars from public git repositories (many open-source projects and sample packs check them in) and from the DAW vendor's free trial download, whose bundled library ships thousands of `.adg`/`.alc` files and `.asd` sidecars beside its sample WAVs. Record each file's origin and licence in the design note; keep the fixtures small and never commit audio.
2. **Test material.** Every test and every conformance check runs against samples and manifests from the production library (sync it down read-only; never push). There is plenty and it grows hourly, so pick a fixed, named handful for determinism.
3. **Acceptance.** Opening the exported file in the DAW needs the DAW installed somewhere. The owner should install the free trial on this Mac when the first acceptance task is reached; until then acceptance tasks stay blocked, not skipped, and the machine-checkable conformance tests are the gate.
